newsitem.title: JAPAN: M'bishi mulls China vehicle joint venture.
newsitem.headline: M'bishi mulls China vehicle joint venture.

text.p: Mitsubishi Motors Corp is considering forming a joint venture in Hunan province, China, for the production of Pajero sport-utility vehicles (SUV), a Mitsubishi spokesman said on Tuesday.

Mitsubishi's Pajero is now being produced at a vehicle plant under the People's Liberation Army in Hunan province with Mitsubishi's technical assistance. The plant is likely to be absorbed by the joint venture, industry sources say.
The vehicle plant received government approval for production in May.

The Mitsubishi spokesman said the company was in talks with officials at the Hunan plant on setting up a joint venture in which the plant would be the partner. But he could not provide any details. "We have not yet received approval for the setting up of a joint venture," he said.
The vehicle plant will produce 1,000 Pajeros in 1996 and is expected to produce 5,000 Pajeros in 1998, the spokesman said.
The South China Morning Post reported on Tuesday that Mitsubishi had received approval to set up a car joint venture in Hunan to produce all-terrain vehicles.
The paper said the approval from the State Planning Commission came even though the central government had said it would not approve any more new foreign-funded car plants.
The paper said Mitsubishi was expected to take a 25 percent stake in the venture and the vehicle plant under the People's Liberation Army would take the remaining stake.
